precepts.text: Give not thy strength to strangers; when thou hast gotten a fruitful possession through all the field, sow it with thine own seed, trusting in the goodness of thy stock, so shall thy race which thou leavest be magnified, having the confidence of their good descent; Israel has every color and feature, so there is no reason to step out.
precepts.point: Put your seed in the womb that belongs to you; a child of mixed seed grows up confused and shunned by both sides.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.why:
“My son, keep the flower of thine age sound; and give not thy strength to strangers.” Your strength is your seed, your legacy. Do not give it to strangers. It is the same thing God said in Malachi: we dealt treacherously against the wife of our youth by giving our seed to Moab and Ammon and Edom.

“When thou hast gotten a fruitful possession through all the field, sow it with thine own seed, trusting in the goodness of thy stock.” The fruitful possession is a woman. The field is the world: our people are found all throughout the world. Sow that fruitful possession with your own seed, and trust in the goodness of your stock, because your woman is your stock; she is your kind. Her womb is the soil that belongs to you, the housing for gods, which is why God made one, “That he might seek a godly seed.”

“So thy race which thou leavest shall be magnified, having the confidence of their good descent.” Your race, your legacy, shall be magnified. The children know that daddy and mommy come from royalty: daddy is Judah, mama is Ephraim, the same nation of people. That child does not grow up confused and lost. Mix your seed with the nations and the child grows up confused, not knowing what it is, and shunned by both sides; it is like forcing a triangle peg into a square hole.

Marry your own and stick with your own people. Israel is a multi-featured, multicolored people, an assortment of beautiful colors and features, so there is no reason to step out of your nation. Wanting to step out means you despise yourself. Even the rich Edomite understands that the womb of our women carries genetic perfection, dominant superior genes.

precepts.text: The Lord hath been witness between thee and the wife of thy youth, thy companion and the wife of thy covenant. God was in the first marriage and is in every marriage. A covenant is a contract of commitment and obligation, not feelings. You understand your phone plan and a sports contract but not this one. Treacherous or not, one flesh is still your companion. She will not be bad forever; hormones change, and you have to be able to live with that person through every dinner, drive, and wake-up.
precepts.point: Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother and cleave unto his wife, and they shall be one flesh. One flesh means inseparable, but not up your wife's skirt all the time as her best friend: without God there is no wife and no family, so the man's priorities stay in God's order. Marriage began as a divine institution, and what we call marriage today is a human invention.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

precepts.why:
In Eden there was no courtship, no feast and no attraction language. God took the rib and made a woman, “and brought her unto the man.” God formed the union himself, and behind that union is a covenant. Malachi shows it: “the Lord hath been witness between thee and the wife of thy youth”. God was the one who did the first marriage, and God is in the midst of every marriage; what God joins together, man is not to put asunder.

The world kept pieces of this. When a minister says, before the Lord and all these witnesses I now pronounce you man and wife, that is a rudiment of what the Bible says, and a rudiment is only a part, not the whole.

A covenant is a contract. People understand contracts: a sports fan understands a player's contract, you understand the contract for your job and the contract for your phone plan, but somehow we do not understand the contract of marriage, which is far more powerful and profound. Covenants are built on commitment and obligation, not feelings: if you do this, then this will happen.

God speaks of the wife “against whom thou hast dealt treacherously: yet is she thy companion, and the wife of thy covenant.” Even if you are being treacherous with your wife, or she with you, you are one flesh, and that is still your companion, the wife of the covenant you made.

Signing a contract on feelings is how people get ripped off buying a car: they like the smell and the color and end up paying the interest rate and the add-ons. Some brothers marry that way: I will deal with all this because she is bad. She is not going to be bad forever. When you get old and the hormones change, you have to be able to live with that person through every dinner, every drive and every wake-up. It has to be stronger than romance and attraction.

Modern ideas about marriage assume feelings are the foundation: find the love of your life, find your prince charming. That is the confusion. The marriage God ordained in Eden stands on his order and on the covenant he witnesses, and that is what carries it through the trials.

precepts.text: The priest's lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth. God's knowledge is his law.
precepts.point: The prophets of Samaria, the northern Latino tribes, prophesied in Baal; the prophets of Jerusalem commit adultery and walk in lies, from December 25 to the ever-virgin Mary, and strengthen the hands of evildoers so the white man can do no wrong. They are all to God as Sodom and Gomorrah.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
The shepherds God sets up feed his people “with knowledge and understanding.” Knowledge and understanding of what? Malachi breaks it down: “For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.”

There is that word knowledge again, and it is joined to the law. God's knowledge is his law. So the shepherds of Jeremiah 23:4 feed the flock with God's laws.

That is exactly what the pastors of today do not do. They teach that the law is done away with, and so both prophet and priest are profane: treating what is holy as common and unclean, defiling and polluting God's name, his Sabbath and his sanctuary. The true shepherd's lips keep the law, and the people seek it at his mouth.

precepts.text: The priest's lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth.
precepts.point: That which is highly esteemed among men, like shellfish and bacon, is abomination in the sight of God.

note.label: 2025 Recap: Different Times, Same Truth

precepts.why:
“My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge”. What is the knowledge we have rejected? Malachi answers: “For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth”. The knowledge is the law.

So the knowledge is not what you learn at a university; the black woman is the most educated woman on the earth, and that is not the knowledge we are ignorant of. Our people are ignorant of the laws of God. Our people don't understand that today is the Lord's Sabbath, and you are not supposed to be buying and selling, cooking, or playing football, because the white man said every day is the Sabbath. Our women don't understand they are not supposed to wear pants, because that knowledge was taken from them. Our men in America don't know they are not supposed to shave their beards, because the white man said, if you want to look like a man, shave your beard.

We are in a diabolical matrix, deeper than anything the movie could show: everything you were taught is good here in America is bad. That is why Hosea goes on, “seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children.” That is what has happened to us. Our people are at the bottom of society, the mother with her kids living all year for a tax return, the drug dealers, the ball players and the rappers, all in Esau's trick bag, while the man down the street teaching the law is what would disrupt all of it.

precepts.text: Judah hath married the daughter of a strange god.
precepts.point: Those who marry the enemy their fathers fought against bring home the one who oppressed them.

note.label: Political Power Under Darkness

precepts.why:
“Judah hath dealt treacherously, and an abomination is committed in Israel and in Jerusalem; for Judah hath profaned the holiness of the Lord which he loved, and hath married the daughter of a strange god.” By marrying the other nations, Judah profaned the holiness of the Lord. And it is not only Judah; the whole twelve tribes did it.

This is spiritual. Those married to that nation all look bugged the hell out, because they have a different spirit in them, the beast spirit. Look at Serena Williams today, all bleached; she looks crazy because of that beast. You are not supposed to mingle the warrior seed with this beast, or mix the royal seed with pig seed.

So Deuteronomy 7:3 is not about skin alone: “For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods”. Marrying the daughter of a strange god is marrying the other god and taking on another spirit. It is called lust, and in the end the lust fades away.

precepts.text: And now, O ye priests, this commandment is for you; the chapter is spoken to the priests.
precepts.point: That is why leadership today is not walking around requiring Levite lineage of Aaron. Christ is the high priest now, and the nation is a whole nation of kings and priests; Malachi and Hebrews are two good books to study on the changing of the priesthood, against the doctrine that the Aaronic covenant could never change.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

precepts.why:
“And now, O ye priests, this commandment is for you.” The whole chapter is spoken to the priests, the seed of Aaron who were consecrated in Exodus 29 for a perpetual statute.

What happened to that everlasting covenant of the priesthood is answered here, in a commandment aimed straight at the priests themselves.

precepts.text: The covenant with Levi was of life and peace and the priest is the messenger of the Lord of hosts; but ye are departed out of the way, caused many to stumble at the law, and have corrupted the covenant of Levi.
precepts.point: That is why leadership today is not walking around requiring Levite lineage of Aaron. Christ is the high priest now, and the nation is a whole nation of kings and priests; Malachi and Hebrews are two good books to study on the changing of the priesthood, against the doctrine that the Aaronic covenant could never change.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

precepts.why:
“My covenant was with him of life and peace”: the covenant with Levi. “The law of truth was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found in his lips: he walked with me in peace and equity, and did turn many away from iniquity.” That was the priest's office as it was given: “For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.”

“But ye are departed out of the way; ye have caused many to stumble at the law; ye have corrupted the covenant of Levi, saith the Lord of hosts.” The priests were finessing the offerings, keeping the best animals for themselves and sacrificing the blind and the broken, and they perverted the teachings of the law for their own benefit. Both parts of the job Ecclesiasticus lays out, the sacrifices and the teaching, they corrupted.

That is why leadership today is not walking around requiring Levite lineage of Aaron. Christ is the high priest now, and the nation is a whole nation of kings and priests. Malachi and Hebrews are two good books to study on the changing of the priesthood, against the doctrine that the Aaronic covenant could never change.

precepts.text: The priest's lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth; the knowledge the Most High desired is the law.
precepts.point: Jeremiah carries the same word: I spake not unto your fathers concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices, but this thing commanded I them, obey my voice. Yet they hearkened not, but walked in the counsels of their evil heart and went backward and not forward; speak all these words unto them, but they will not hearken. That is seen every sabbath on the streets.

note.label: Leviticus 6: The Trespass Offering and the Fire That Shall Never Go Out

precepts.why:
Malachi says “the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.”

The knowledge of God the Most High desired more than burnt offerings is the law. The priest who kept the fire burning on the altar was also to keep knowledge on his lips, so the people could seek the law at his mouth.

precepts.text: The law of truth was in his mouth, and the priest's lips should keep knowledge, but ye are departed out of the way, ye have caused many to stumble at the law, ye have corrupted the covenant of Levi; therefore have I made you contemptible and base before all the people.
precepts.point: But they corrupted the covenant of Levi, left off teaching the law, and were partial in it, so the Lord gave them a swift and mighty judgment. Now you understand why Levi, identified in the land of Haiti, has been the poorest in the western hemisphere and catches hell to this day: their provider was the Lord, and they departed out of the way.

note.label: Deuteronomy 10: What Doth the Lord Require of Thee

precepts.why:
At that time the Lord separated the tribe of Levi “to bear the ark of the covenant of the Lord, to stand before the Lord to minister unto him, and to bless in his name”, and “Levi hath no part nor inheritance with his brethren; the Lord is his inheritance”. Malachi shows what that covenant looked like when it was kept: “The law of truth was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found in his lips: he walked with me in peace and equity, and did turn many away from iniquity. For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.”

Levi ate well through the sacrifices the Lord set up. The Levites dwelt in the best areas, the suburbs, and lived in castles, because the Lord was their provider. All they had to do was teach Israel the commandments of God: keep knowledge on their lips, and let Israel seek the law at their mouth.

“But ye are departed out of the way; ye have caused many to stumble at the law; ye have corrupted the covenant of Levi, saith the Lord of hosts. Therefore have I also made you contemptible and base before all the people, according as ye have not kept my ways, but have been partial in the law.” They left off teaching the law and were partial in it, so the Lord gave them a swift and mighty judgment: contemptible and base before all the people.

Now you understand why Levi, identified in the land of Haiti, has been the poorest in the western hemisphere and catches hell to this day. Their provider was the Lord, and they departed out of the way.

precepts.text: The priest's lips keep knowledge, so knowledge is tied to the law and the commandments.
precepts.point: Attend to wisdom and bow your ear to understanding so that you may regard knowledge. The knowledge spoken of here is the commandments of the Most High.

note.label: Proverbs 5: The Strange Woman and Thy Labours in the House of a Stranger

precepts.why:
“My son, attend unto my wisdom, and bow thine ear to my understanding: That thou mayest regard discretion, and that thy lips may keep knowledge.” The knowledge spoken of here is the commandments of the Most High.

Malachi shows that: “For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.” The priest's lips keep knowledge, and what is sought at his mouth is the law. Knowledge is tied to the law and the commandments.

So lips that keep knowledge are lips that keep the law. Attend to wisdom and bow your ear to understanding so that you may regard knowledge, which is the commandments.

precepts.text: The priest's lips should keep knowledge, and the people seek the law at his mouth.
precepts.point: We are the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth, and we must learn to behave ourselves and possess our vessels, constrained from sin.

note.label: Isaiah 33: The Lord Our Judge, Lawgiver, and King

precepts.why:
Wisdom and knowledge are the commandments, and they are kept in a certain place: “For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.”

The priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and the people seek the law at his mouth, because he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts. So the knowledge that is “the stability of thy times” is the law, kept on the priest’s lips and sought there by the people. That is how the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth, learns to behave itself: seeking the law at the mouth of the one who keeps it, in the fear of the Lord that is his treasure.

precepts.text: The priest's lips should keep knowledge, for knowledge is God's laws, which the pastor is supposed to feed the people.
precepts.point: He will give pastors according to His heart to feed us with knowledge and understanding; a pastor is supposed to feed us with the laws of God, so if your pastor is not feeding you God's laws, you need to run.

note.label: Jeremiah 3: Backsliding Israel Called to Return

precepts.why:
The Lord promises to give “pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding.” Malachi shows what that knowledge is: “For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.”

Knowledge is God's laws. The people are to seek the law at the priest's mouth, so a pastor according to his heart is one who feeds us with the laws of God. If your pastor is not feeding you God's laws, you need to run. The pastor he gives to the backsliding children he brings to Zion is the messenger of the Lord of hosts, and his lips keep the law.

precepts.text: The priest's lips should keep knowledge, so a man must deal with his wife and household according to the scripture.
precepts.point: To be full of the Holy Ghost is first and foremost to be keeping the laws. The office is desired by your works, your dedication, and your natural love for your people, not by gunning for a title. Moses was made a leader because he defended his people, and David showed the attributes of a leader wrestling lions and bears and facing Goliath before he was ever called.

note.label: Acts 6: The Grecians Were Greek-Speaking Israelites

precepts.why:
“For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.”

To be full of the Holy Ghost is first and foremost to be keeping the laws. The people seek the law at the priest's mouth, so a man must deal with his wife and household according to the scripture before he is set over the business of the body.
